problem: LLM-based navigation decision models show a decision bias in indoor dynamic scenes: they favor short-term risk avoidance over long-term path optimization, and traditional discrete RL models lag in success rate and decision delay.
motivation: Indoor dynamic environments with moving obstacles require both immediate collision avoidance and efficient long-horizon planning. Integrating large models with navigation is in demand, but fixed reward trade-offs between the two objectives lead to biased decisions.
key_idea: Fine-tune Llama3-7B with PPO under a VLN-R1-style reinforcement fine-tuning paradigm, using a time-decay reward whose exponential coefficient dynamically weights immediate obstacle avoidance against long-term path planning.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablations can be cited. The claim is that a time-decay reward, which prioritizes short-term risk responses when danger is imminent, balances the two objectives better than discrete RL. It reports a 5.7% higher dynamic-avoidance success rate and 6.2% lower decision delay.
method: Perception-decision-feedback closed loop: multimodal navigation data is the input and the LLM outputs decisions, with feedback from the environment.

Time-decay reward function: an exponential decay coefficient dynamically allocates reward weight between immediate obstacle avoidance and long-term path planning, prioritizing short-term risk responses.
PPO reinforcement fine-tuning: the base LLM (Llama3 7B) is fine-tuned with PPO following the VLN-R1 paradigm to adapt to dynamic navigation decision logic.

setting.training_data: Unspecified in the abstract; a dynamic-obstacle indoor navigation dataset ("the dataset") is used

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports relative gains (+5.7% dynamic obstacle avoidance success rate, -6.2% decision delay, 84.3% semantic satisfaction rate in high dynamic density), but no absolute metrics on a canonical benchmark.
results: Compared with traditional discrete RL models, TDR-LLM-RFT improves dynamic obstacle avoidance success rate by 5.7% and reduces decision delay by 6.2%. It retains an 84.3% semantic satisfaction rate in high dynamic density scenes.
limitations: Evaluated on an unspecified in-house dataset, with no standard benchmark reported.
The baseline is only traditional discrete RL, with no comparison to other LLM/VLN methods stated.
Simulator, real-robot validation and the action space are not described, so it is unclear how well the results transfer.
